column9: COVID-era 2020 distribution; district received ~4,000 devices (Chromebooks for older students + touchpads for younger) plus ~500 additional Chromebooks; funded via CARES Act; ~9,500 students; ~700 Dell laptops also distributed to teachers; prior to 2020 no 1:1 evidence found

District purchased ~9,000 Chromebooks for all students gr 3+; distributed November 2016 (most schools after holiday break); ~$1.8M expenditure at <$200/device; Clay-Battelle HS had used Chromebooks ~3 years prior to district-wide rollout; funded by excess levy dollars

Upper bound; district Chromebook page exists with support info; NC statewide federal pandemic funding drove 1:1 expansion; no pre-2020 firm rollout year found for Lee County specifically; likely COVID-era full 1:1 deployment

District began buying Chromebooks May 2012; by Apr 2015 had ~95 devices; by Nov 2015 ~2,000 Chromebooks; completed 1:1 ratio ~2018-19 via Governor's Office of Student Achievement grants ($466,650 in Jan 2018 + $520,175 in prior rounds); 1:1 completed for all gr3-12 with grant completion; PreK-2 remain classroom sets

Upper bound; Forward Learning 1:1 Technology Program covers all students gr 3-11 with personal laptop for school and home; program page confirmed on district site but no firm launch year found in web sources; 2020 upper bound based on current confirmed 1:1 program evidence

Upper bound; district provides loaner Chromebooks and mobile MiFi to students lacking personal computer; UTICA TEAM (Technology Experiences And Media) program for library/ed tech; 2020 COVID-era loaner Chromebook program confirmed; district's 2018-19 IT plan indicated 2020 as target for take-home devices; no firm pre-2020 1:1 launch date found

Future Ready 1:1 initiative; over 6,000 new devices purchased in 2020-21 school year doubling district device total; program provides iPad for K-1 and Chromebook gr2-12; 4-year recycle program; COVID-era launch confirmed; goal of 1:1 always existed; pandemic accelerated full deployment

Going G.L.O.B.A.L. (Growing Learning Opportunities Beyond All Limits) initiative launched 2010-11; 1:1 access: iPad for K-8 students; MacBook Air for gr9-12; district recognized as Apple Distinguished Program starting 2012 and again 2013 and 2015-16; one of early NC districts for full K-12 1:1

1:1 initiative launched 2014-15 SY under Supt Tim Wilder; 7,000+ devices distributed; started with iPads; board voted to switch to Chromebooks for 2017-18 SY for cost savings (~half the price) and Google Apps compatibility; strong pre-existing Google Drive usage by teachers drove switch

column7: 2014-15: Penn HS; 2015-16: all 3 MS; ES classroom use
column9: HP Chromebook 11 issued to all Penn HS students starting 2014-15 SY; all 3 middle schools followed in 2015-16; elementary students use Chromebooks in classrooms during school day; ~$80/yr student fee; K-5 iPads added; currently gr 6-12 (~6,000 students) get take-home Chromebook

Every student TK-12 equipped by 2020-21 SY launch (Aug 17 2020); district confirmed 'every one of our students has a device' for distance learning start; iPad for TK-1; Chromebook gr2-12; COVID-era universal deployment; prior to 2020 no evidence of district-wide 1:1

One-to-One Technology initiative launched 2013; district provides each student with own tablet for ready access to curriculum and instructional tools; Sunnyvale SD is a K-8 district (TK-5 elementary + 6-8 middle); 2013 is confirmed launch year per district's own 1:1 technology page

column7: District-wide ratio 1.8:1; Fillmore ES and Maple HS at 1:1; Lompoc HS near 2:1
column9: Upper bound; June 2016 article describes district 'technology revolution' with 665 Lenovo ThinkPad tablets + 600 Toshiba Chromebooks + 700 Dell laptops for teachers; two campuses at 1:1 but district-wide ratio only 1.8:1 as of 2016; not yet full district-wide 1:1; classified Partial

May 2019 board approved accelerating 1:1 initiative; all gr6-12 students issued Chromebook for 2019-20 SY; by 2025-26 expanded to gr4-12; students submit signed forms and insurance payment before school; dedicated 1:1 Learning Initiative website maintained by district

Upper bound; MillerShift Initiative provides iPad to all K-12 students; district confirmed 'an iPad for every student' K-12; 5th Grade 1:1 Initiative page suggests phased rollout starting with 5th grade; firm launch year not confirmed via web search; upper bound 2020 based on confirmed full K-12 program

March 2020 COVID closure drove distribution of ~5,000 Chromebooks (roughly half district enrollment); secondary level has established 1:1 Chromebook agreement; devices issued to all enrolled students upon enrollment; Google Workspace used district-wide; pre-2020 secondary Chromebook 1:1 program existed but full take-home expanded with COVID

Board approved ~$1.9M lease for iPads and Dell laptops for every student in July 2020 for COVID virtual learning; iPads for K-5; Dell laptops for gr6-12; supply chain issues delayed some devices (older Chromebooks/HP laptops used temporarily); September 2021 formal 1:1 program expansion approved

column9: June 2014 board decision: middle schools to receive Chromebooks (except Chute+King Arts which got Digital Promise iPads); Chromebooks for gr3-5 students confirmed; K-2 and some MS use iPads; MacBooks for specialized curriculum; 2014-15 SY rollout for MS grades; ongoing expansion to reach all grades

column7: Classroom-based blended learning; partial 1:1 at HS

Always Initiative (1:1 Device Program); phased rollout: 2012 gr3-5 tablets at Martin ES; 2013 all ES K-5 tablets; 2014 MS gr6-7 Chromebooks; 2016 all HS + remaining students — fully K-12 by Fall 2016; largest K-12 1:1 district in Illinois at completion; Google Workspace since 2013; device upgrades at grades 1/3/6/9
